Definition: by implication, of falling); desire; also ruin
BiblicalUsage: Havvah is desire that has curdled into ruin, craving that destroys, and the Bible uses it for both. In Job 6:2 it is Job's calamity, in Proverbs 10:3 it is the craving of the wicked that God casts away, in Psalms 5:9 it is the destruction in the mouth of liars, and in Micah 7:3 the great man utters his mischievous desire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is a warning about what desire becomes when it is left to itself: it starts as wanting and ends as wreckage. The psalmist shows me the same mouth can carry ruin, and I want mine to carry something else.
